_note: WAISentry incident case files for the fictional client Kitewing Software (tokenised). Synthetic.

incidents.title: Consent phishing -> hidden mail forwarding -> vendor payment-diversion (BEC) attempt
attack_path: Consent-phishing email 'Shared document: Q4 vendor remittance' from a 2-day-old domain (01:58)
User granted the unverified 'PDF Secure Viewer' app mail-read, mail-settings and full-Drive scopes (02:04)
App added an external forwarding address and a finance-keyword filter (02:05)
Filter skips the inbox and marks messages read, so the user never sees replies
Password sign-in from Amsterdam 8 minutes after a Cedar Harbor sign-in — stopped by the security key (02:06)
412 messages read through the Gmail API (02:06)
Lookalike-vendor email asks AP to change bank details for open invoice TD-2026-1187 (02:07)
Public links created on 2 Confidential finance files (02:07)
analyst_checklist: Is 'PDF Secure Viewer' an approved app?
No — unverified publisher, domain 2 days old, not on the allowlist
Did anyone else grant it?
No — 1 grant; the 2 other recipients did not click
Did the Amsterdam sign-in succeed?
No — the security-key challenge failed
What left through the forwarding rule?
1 message (the attacker's own bank-change email)
Which files were exposed?
38 downloaded through the API; 2 public links, 0 external views
Is a payment due to the impersonated vendor?
Yes — TD-2026-1187, $48,600, due 2026-11-10: finance must hold it
Was internal phishing sent from the mailbox?
No messages sent through the app

recommended_playbooks.why: end every web session and token the attacker may hold
revoke the app tenant-wide and block its client id
suspend 4 h until the password is reset (security key kept)

escalate: Remove the forwarding filter and forwarding address (mail-rule change is not pre-approved)
Hold payment of TD-2026-1187 and verify the vendor's bank details by phone on file (client finance)
Block tessaro-designs.example, securedoc-viewer.example and relaymail.example in Mimecast and DNSFilter (client approval)
client_actions: Analyst A-17 phoned Noah Kim (client on-call) and paged Marcus Bell for the payment hold
Noah Kim removed the filter and forwarding address
Password reset; account unsuspended at 06:10 after the user confirmed by phone
Marcus Bell verified with Tessaro by phone: no bank change; TD-2026-1187 paid to the account on file on 2026-11-04
Third-party app access restricted: unverified apps blocked, 14-app allowlist
incidents.outcome: Contained in 29 s after analyst confirmation; payment diversion of $48,600 prevented; $0 lost; no external views of the public links.
incidents.contained_by: pre-approved playbooks PB-01, PB-02, PB-04, PB-03

incidents.title: Infostealer on a support laptop -> stolen session cookie replay (blocked)
attack_path: User ran 'pdfconvert_setup.exe' downloaded from a 17-day-old PDF-converter site (14:18)
Unsigned process read the Chrome login-data store (14:21)
...and the cookie store, stealing live web-session cookies
Stolen cookie replayed from Frankfurt at 14:31 — rejected, sessions already revoked at 14:24
Stolen password tried at 14:31 — security key and suspension blocked it
analyst_checklist: Is the EDR detection a true positive?
Yes — unsigned binary read browser credential and cookie stores
Was data sent out?
Yes — 4.1 MB to a hosting IP: assume cookies and saved passwords are stolen
Which accounts are exposed?
The user's Workspace session + 4 saved SaaS passwords
Is the device still online?
Yes — isolation needs the client (not pre-approved)

recommended_playbooks.why: invalidate every stolen session cookie and token
suspend 4 h until the password is reset

escalate: Isolate the laptop with the EDR console (device isolation is not pre-approved)
Rotate the 4 saved SaaS passwords and reset the Workspace password (client IT)
client_actions: Analyst A-09 called Hugo Laurent (Millbrook IT)
Hugo Laurent isolated the laptop in the EDR console
Passwords rotated; freepdfconvert-pro.example blocked in DNSFilter
incidents.outcome: Sessions revoked 7 minutes before the attacker tried the stolen cookie; replay and password sign-in both failed; no data accessed in Workspace.

incidents.title: Confidential customer ARR export shared publicly and to a personal mailbox
attack_path: Confidential export (171 customer rows with ARR) set to 'anyone with the link' (09:04)
Same file shared with a personal mailbox (09:04)
analyst_checklist: Malicious or accidental?
Accidental — the owner is preparing case-study numbers; no other risky activity
Was the link opened externally?
No — 0 external views so far
Is the file Confidential?
Yes — label Confidential, customer ARR for 171 accounts

recommended_playbooks.why: remove the public link and the personal-mailbox share

escalate: Tell the user's manager (Alicia Moreau) and remind the user of the sharing policy (client)
Change the Marketing OU default link sharing to 'restricted' (domain setting — client admin)
incidents.outcome: Open: PB-04 recommended; no external views yet.

incidents.title: Payroll-lure credential-harvest phishing wave (no compromise)
attack_path: 14 users received 'Payroll portal: confirm your direct deposit' from payroll-kitewing.example
1 click (page blocked by DNSFilter, phishing category); 6 users reported it with the KnowBe4 button
analyst_checklist: Did anyone enter credentials?
No — the only click was blocked at DNS
escalate: Purge the 14 messages from mailboxes with Mimecast (message purge is not pre-approved)
client_actions: Noah Kim approved the purge in chat
incidents.outcome: No compromise; 14 messages purged 8 minutes after the first report.

events.detail: 3 users reported the message with the Phish Alert Button within 90 s

incidents.contained_by: escalation — analyst purged the messages after client approval

incidents.title: MFA-fatigue push bombing against a contractor account
incidents.actor_role: QA Engineer (contractor, Google prompt — security key pending)
attack_path: Password from a third-party breach used from 198.51.100.140 (Singapore, hosting)
11 Google prompts in 4 minutes; the user denied all of them
analyst_checklist: Did any prompt get approved?
No — 11 denied
Is the password known to the attacker?
Yes — reset needed

recommended_playbooks.why: end any session, just in case
suspend 4 h to stop the prompts until the password is reset

escalate: Reset the password and ship a security key (client IT)
incidents.outcome: Prompts stopped within 4 minutes of the first one; no sign-in succeeded.

events.detail: 5th Google prompt in 150 s after correct passwords from 198.51.100.140 (Singapore, hosting); all denied

incidents.title: Legacy remote-access tool on the Millbrook file server beaconing to a re-registered domain
attack_path: 'LegacyRemote 6' support agent left by a former IT provider tried to self-update
Update domain had changed owner (re-registered 2026-10-20); DNSFilter and the IDS blocked it
analyst_checklist: Did any connection succeed?
No — blocked at DNS and at the firewall
escalate: Uninstall LegacyRemote 6 from MB-FS01 (server change — client IT, business hours)
incidents.outcome: Blocked by preventive controls in real time; tool removed the same morning.

events.detail: MB-FS01 lookup of update-check.cdn-mirror.example blocked (newly registered / malware)
IDS signature 'LegacyRemote outdated agent update' — outbound connection blocked at MB-FW01

incidents.contained_by: preventive controls — DNSFilter and the IDS blocked the beacon

incidents.title: Password spray against the Millbrook domain controller from an end-of-life reception PC
incidents.actor_role: Reception PC (Windows 10, out of support, no EDR)
attack_path: 312 failed Kerberos pre-authentications against 41 AD accounts in 11 minutes from MB-WS07
analyst_checklist: Any successful logon?
No
Is the source host managed?
No EDR, Windows 10 out of support
escalate: Isolate MB-WS07 from the network (on-prem device isolation is not pre-approved)
client_actions: Hugo Laurent disabled the switch port (P2 phone escalation)
PC removed; forensic image found a commodity loader from a USB stick
incidents.outcome: No account compromised; 41 minutes from confirmation to isolation because on-prem isolation needs the client.

events.detail: Burst of failed Kerberos pre-authentication (4771) and logon failures (4625) on MB-DC01 for 41 accounts from MB-WS07

incidents.contained_by: escalation — client IT disabled the switch port
